t: The Treaty of Lausanne of 24 July 1923 won international recognition for the Turkish state as the Ottoman Empire's successor, and the Republic was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the new capital.

Mustafa Kemal's reforms turned a religion-based, multi-communal monarchy into a secular nation state: a civil code based on the Swiss code in 1926, the alphabet reform, and the vote for women in 1934.

Turkey joined NATO in 1952 after fighting in the Korean War and keeps the alliance's second-largest military; coups or memorandums in 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997 broke its multiparty politics, and a 2017 referendum made it a presidential republic.
dyk: Non-Muslims were 19.1% of the population of what is now Turkey in 1914 and 2.5% by 1927, after the genocides of the war years and the population exchange with Greece; today they are about 0.2%.
ev: The Republic is proclaimed in Ankara after the Treaty of Lausanne and the withdrawal of the last Allied troops from Istanbul on 4 October; Mustafa Kemal becomes its first president.
Women gain the right to vote nationally; the Surname Law gives Mustafa Kemal the name Atatürk.
Atatürk dies and İsmet İnönü becomes the second president; Turkey stays neutral in almost all of the Second World War.
After fighting with the UN forces in the Korean War, Turkey joins NATO as a bulwark against Soviet expansion into the Mediterranean.
The third military coup, after those of 1960 and 1971; the constitution still in force is approved by referendum in 1982.
Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's Justice and Development Party (AKP) wins power, beginning more than two decades of AKP government.
On 15 July an attempted coup fails; by 2024 the government counts 13,251 people jailed in connection with it.
A referendum replaces the parliamentary republic with an executive presidency and abolishes the office of prime minister.

f.founder: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, leader of the Turkish National Movement and the republic's first president
f.predecessor: The Ottoman Empire, whose sultanate the Ankara parliament abolished on 1 November 1922, and the Government of the Grand National Assembly in Ankara (from 23 April 1920)
